Order 
This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-Insurance Company challenging the award dated 04/04/2019 passed by the First Additional Motor Claims Tribunal, Ambah District Morena (M.P.) in Claim Case No. 64/2016,
whereby compensation has been awarded to the claimants.

sentences.text: The appellant seeks reduction of the amount of compensation so awarded.
2. The date of the accident, the finding of negligence, and the liability of the Insurance Company are not in dispute.

The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal on these aspects have attained finality,
as the same have not been assailed in the present appeal.

along with interest from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization on account of the death of Sarnam Singh.

1 4. Brief facts of the case are that respondent Nos. 1 and 2, who are brothers of the deceased Sarnam Singh, filed a claim petition before the Claims Tribunal stating that on 11.09.2012, the deceased was standing on the Ambah-Morena road and talking to one Bhikaram when a bus bearing registration No. MP06-P-0162, driven rashly and negligently by respondent No. 4, dashed against him, resulting in his death on the spot.
A criminal case was registered at Police Station Ambah against the driver.
5. The appellant-Insurance Company filed its written statement contending that the claimants were not dependent upon the deceased and, therefore, were not entitled to compensation.
6. The Claims Tribunal, after framing issues and appreciating the evidence on record, allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation as stated above.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that both the claimants are major, married, and living separately with their respective families.
They are earning members and are capable of maintaining themselves.
Therefore, they cannot be treated as dependents of the deceased, and the Tribunal erred in awarding compensation under the head of loss of dependency.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 and 2/claimants NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10682 3 MA-3563-2019 supported the impugned award and placed reliance upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Montford Brothers of St. Gabriel and another Vs United India Insurance Company Ltd and another, 2014 ACJ 667 , wherein it has been held that being legal representatives of the deceased, they are entitled to compensation.

entities.text: Montford Brothers of St. Gabriel and another Vs United India Insurance Company Ltd and another, 2014 ACJ 667
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record of the Claims Tribunal.
10. It is undisputed that the claimants are brothers of the deceased and are aged about 40 and 44 years, respectively.
11. Claimant No. 1, Suresh Chandra, admitted in his cross-examination that he is engaged in agricultural work, earns his livelihood, and is capable of maintaining his family.
Similarly, claimant No. 2, Murarilal, also admitted that he is an earning member, married, and has a family comprising his wife and six children, whom he maintains.
12. From the evidence on record, it is clear that both the claimants are living separately and are financially independent.

13. In the case of Amrit Bhanu Shali and others Vs National Insurance Co.
Ltd. and others, 2012 ACJ 2002 in para No. 16 has been held as under :-
Admittedly both the parents, Ist appellant- Amrit Bhanu Shali (father) and 2nd appellant- Smt. Sarlaben (mother) have been held to be dependents of deceased- Ritesh Bhanu Shali and, therefore, the Tribunal held that the Ist appellant and 2nd appellant have the right to get the compensation.

sentences.text:
In these circumstances,
she is not found to be dependent upon the deceased.

Thus, both the parents being dependents, i.e., father and the mother, the Tribunal rightly restricted the 'personal and living expenses' of the deceased to 50% and contribution to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10682 4 MA-3563-2019

the family was required to be taken as 50% as per the decision of this Court in the case of Sarla Verma, 2009 ACJ 198 (SC)
14.

In view of the aforesaid legal position, it is evident that a married daughter living separately and maintained by her earning husband cannot be treated as a dependent upon her deceased mother or brother.
In the present case, two brothers/claimants who are living separately and they are able to maintain themselves and their family, cannot be treated as a dependent upon brother.

15. In the case of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs Anand Pal and others, 2024 ACJ 6 ,it was held that if brothers of deceased was living seperately with their respective families then they are not dependent upon deceased and they are not entitled to get compensation.

entities.text: New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs Anand Pal and others, 2024 ACJ 6
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 16. This Court is of the considered view that although the claimants are legal representatives of the deceased, they were neither wholly nor partially dependent upon deceased.
Consequently, the Claims Tribunal committed an error in treating the claimants as a dependent and awarding compensation on that basis.
17. However, the claimants, being a legal representative, are entitled to compensation under the conventional heads, namely, no-fault liability and funeral expenses, as permissible under law.
18. In respect of the death of Sarnam, the claimants are entitled Rs. 30,000/- under the head of funeral expenses and Rs. 50,000/- towards no- fault liability.

19. Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation payable in the present case is Rs. 80,000/- as against Rs. 5,08,750/- awarded by the Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10682 5 MA-3563-2019 Tribunal.
20. Accordingly, the compensation amount is reduced from Rs.5,08,750/- to Rs. 80,000/-.
The said amount shall carry interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till its realization.
21. All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain undisturbed.
The Insurance Company shall be entitled to recover the excess amount, if any, already deposited, from the Claims Tribunal in accordance with law.

22. In view of the foregoing discussion, the miscellaneous appeal filed by the Insurance Company stands disposed of accordingly (HIRDESH) JUDGE Prachi National Insurance Company vs Suresh Chandra on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119909868/
